title: Riga: Art Nouveau, Market Halls & the Daugava

summary: A seven-day city trip itinerary in Riga & the Gulf of Riga, Latvia.

itinerary.title: Vecrīga: the Old Town block
itinerary.morning: Airport bus 22 into town, 30 minutes. Begin at Doma laukums with Riga Cathedral, the largest medieval church in the Baltics, and its 6,700-pipe organ.
itinerary.afternoon: The House of the Blackheads, a reconstructed Hanseatic guild house with an outrageous Dutch Renaissance facade, then St Peter's Church for the lift to the 72 m spire viewing platform, the definitive Riga panorama.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in the Old Town, then a beer in Folkklubs Ala Pagrabs, a cellar with Latvian folk music, local ciders and a crowd that is genuinely local despite the location.

itinerary.title: The Quiet Centre: Art Nouveau block
itinerary.morning: Alberta iela is the reason this city is on UNESCO's list: a single street of Mikhail Eisenstein facades with screaming masks, peacocks, sphinxes and blue-tiled reliefs. Walk it slowly, then Elizabetes iela and Strēlnieku iela.
itinerary.afternoon: The Riga Art Nouveau Museum in a restored 1903 apartment, the only place you see how these buildings were actually lived in, down to the kitchen and the servant's stair. Then the Latvian National Museum of Art in its neo-Baroque palace on the edge of the Esplanade.
itinerary.evening: Miera iela, "the street of peace", for the city's independent coffee roastery, a chocolate factory, small bars and a distinctly unpolished bohemian energy.

itinerary.title: Central Market and the Moscow Suburb
itinerary.morning: Riga Central Market: five converted Zeppelin hangars from the First World War, one of the largest markets in Europe. Dairy hall, fish hall, meat hall, and the produce rows outside. Eat breakfast here, grey peas with bacon, smoked fish, rye bread, curd cheese.
itinerary.afternoon: Behind the market, the Latvian Academy of Sciences, a Stalinist skyscraper known locally as "Stalin's birthday cake", with a 17th-floor open observation terrace that costs a few euros and beats every other viewpoint in the city. Continue into the Maskavas forštate, the old wooden Moscow Suburb, sobering and half-abandoned.
itinerary.evening: The Spīķeri warehouse quarter beside the market for dinner and a riverside walk.

itinerary.title: Left bank: Āgenskalns, Kalnciema and wooden Riga
itinerary.morning: Cross the Daugava. Āgenskalns Market and the wooden residential streets around it are what Riga looked like before the boulevards.
itinerary.afternoon: The Kalnciema Quarter, a restored block of 19th-century wooden buildings that hosts a Saturday farmers' and craft market, time this day for a Saturday if you can. Then the Latvian National Library, Gunnar Birkerts' "Castle of Light", whose reading terraces give the classic skyline view back across the river.
itinerary.evening: Return over the bridge at dusk; the Old Town spires from the left bank at sunset are the postcard.

itinerary.title: Jūrmala and the pine coast
itinerary.morning: Commuter train from Riga Central to Majori, about 35 minutes. Jūrmala is a 25 km strip of white sand and pine forest with 4,000 wooden dachas, an aristocratic spa town first, a Soviet resort second, and now something in between.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk Jomas iela, then the beach itself as far as Dubulti and its modernist 1977 railway station. Dzintari forest park has a viewing tower over the canopy.
itinerary.evening: Spa treatment at one of the Jūrmala sanatorium-hotels, or a seafood dinner and the train back.

itinerary.title: Sigulda and the Gauja valley
itinerary.morning: Train to Sigulda, about 1 h 15. Turaida Castle's red-brick tower over the Gauja valley, the Dainu Hill sculpture park of Latvian folk songs, and Gūtmaņa cave with its centuries of carved graffiti.
itinerary.afternoon: The cable car across the valley, and Krimulda. In autumn this valley is the best foliage in the Baltics; in winter it has a bobsleigh track you can ride.
itinerary.evening: Back to Riga. Last dinner at one of the city's ambitious modern-Latvian kitchens, Latvia's restaurant scene has gained significant international recognition in recent years. `verify: true`

itinerary.title: Mežaparks or the Occupation Museum, then out
itinerary.morning: Choose: Mežaparks, Europe's first garden city (planned 1901), with wooden villas under pines and the vast Song Festival stage; or the Museum of the Occupation of Latvia in the centre, which explains the 20th century that made this city.

accommodationStrategy.name: Grand Poet / Neiburgs
accommodationStrategy.location: Old Town and Quiet Centre edge
accommodationStrategy.description: Neiburgs occupies a 1903 Art Nouveau building in the Old Town, you sleep inside the architecture you came to look at, with apartment-style rooms. Grand Poet sits on the Esplanade side, closest to Alberta iela and the museums.

accommodationStrategy.name: Quiet Centre boutique apartments
accommodationStrategy.description: The residential blocks north of Elizabetes iela are quiet, elegant, and full of well-restored apartments at €70-110 a night. Best value in the city and a five-minute walk to both the Art Nouveau district and the Old Town.

accommodationStrategy.name: Āgenskalns / left-bank guesthouses
accommodationStrategy.description: Cheaper still, wooden-house neighbourhood, tram straight over the bridge. Choose this if you want the version of Riga that residents actually live in, and if the Kalnciema Saturday market is a fixed point in your week.

logistics.emergency: 112. Riga's East Clinical University Hospital is the main facility. Pharmacies (*aptieka*) are plentiful; some in the centre run 24 hours.
logistics.weather: Cold continental winters (−5 to −15 °C, dark by 16:00 in December), warm humid summers up to 28 °C. Spring arrives late, April is still bare.
logistics.bookingWindows: Hotels: 4-6 weeks; much longer for the Song and Dance Festival, held every five years, when the city fills completely. `verify: true` Top restaurants: 2-4 weeks. Jūrmala spa treatments: a week.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards are accepted almost everywhere, but the Central Market's produce rows are cash-friendlier and haggling is normal for volume.

other.label: Transit
other.text: One integrated tram, trolleybus and bus network. Buy an e-talons at a kiosk or tap a contactless card. Trams are the useful mode, routes 2, 5 and 10 cover most of this itinerary.

other.label: Language
other.text: Latvian is the state language; Russian is widely spoken and this is a live political subject. English is standard in hospitality and near-universal under 40.

other.label: Stag-party zones
other.text: Parts of the Old Town around Kaļķu iela have an aggressive nightlife economy with a long history of tourist overcharging. Check prices before ordering, avoid street touts for clubs entirely, and drink where locals do, Miera iela, Spīķeri, Kalnciema.

proTips: The **Academy of Sciences terrace** costs a fraction of St Peter's tower, has no queue, and gives you the view *including* the Old Town rather than from inside it. Go 90 minutes before sunset.
Central Market at **08:00** is a working market; at 12:00 it is a tourist attraction. The dairy hall before nine is one of the best food experiences in this dataset.
Time your week so Day 4 lands on a **Saturday** for the Kalnciema Quarter market.
Riga Black Balsam is the local herbal bitter and is punishing neat. The blackcurrant version, or a spoonful in coffee, is how Latvians actually drink it.
The Art Nouveau facades are all above eye level. Walk Alberta iela **twice**, once looking up, once looking at doorways and stairwell glass, which is where the real detail is.
Combine Days 5 and 6 differently if the weather turns: Jūrmala is a fair-weather day, Sigulda works in rain, and the museums absorb a whole wet afternoon.

raw.walkability: High. Old Town, the Quiet Centre and the Central Market are one continuous 3 km walk; Āgenskalns and Kalnciema need a tram or a short taxi
raw.transit_pass: Rīgas Satiksme e-talons card, or contactless; trams, trolleybuses and buses on one system
raw.architectural_focus: The largest concentration of Art Nouveau architecture in the world, roughly a third of central Riga's buildings, plus wooden suburbs and Stalinist monumentalism
